## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kaṅkhārevata Sutta* (Ud 5.7; PTS Ud 60) is a discourse in the fifth chapter of the Udāna [SuttaCentral]. The sutta is set at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove at Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery [Anandajoti Bhikkhu 2007; Masefield 1997]. Venerable Kaṅkhārevata ("Doubting Revata") sits in meditation near the Buddha with legs crossed and body upright, reviewing his own purification achieved by crossing over doubt [Anandajoti Bhikkhu 2007; Masefield 1997; SuttaCentral]. As noted by Anālayo, the commentary explains that Revata had originally received this nickname due to excessive anxiety and scruples regarding Vinaya rules before successfully putting an end to all doubts [Analayo]. Observing Kaṅkhārevata immersed in meditation on his purity, the Buddha utters an inspired verse declaring that the noble, pure one who sees the peril in the world and knows the state free from clinging takes no delight in evil deeds [Anandajoti Bhikkhu 2007; Masefield 1997].
SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels to the verse in various recensions of the *Udānavarga*, including the Sanskrit UV 29 and UVS 29 (*Yugavarga*), the Tibetan translation Uv Kg 29, and Chinese translations T 212.30 and T 213.29 [SuttaCentral]. Kaṅkhārevata's realization is also referenced in the *Therāpadāna* (Tha-Ap 544) and the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.3) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus documents substantial Pali-internal text reuse with 13 other Udāna discourses, primarily consisting of the formulaic prose description of a senior monk meditating upright before the Buddha (§§1.1–4.1), shared with texts such as the *Taṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (Ud 7.6), *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 3.4), *Sāriputtaupasama Sutta* (Ud 4.10), *Mahāmoggallāna Sutta* (Ud 3.5), *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10), and *Subhūti Sutta* (Ud 6.7) [DharmaNexus].
